alternate_names: Tomb and Mosque of Murshid Quli Khan

history.summary: Built in 1723-1724 by Nawab Murshid Quli Khan (founder of Murshidabad, capital moved here from Dhaka in 1717), designed by architect Murad Farash Khan as the new capital's Jami mosque. 'Katra' means marketplace, after the market that surrounded it. One of the largest caravanserais in the Indian subcontinent: a vast courtyard enclosed by double-storied domed cells that housed up to 700 Quran readers (a madrasa), with five domes and four 70-ft minarets. The Nawab's tomb lies under the entrance staircase. Damaged by the 1897 earthquake (two domes and two minarets destroyed); protected as a Monument of National Importance by the ASI since 1910. Inactive as a place of worship. NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed.

name: Katra Mosque
town_description: Murshidabad was the capital of the Nawabs of Bengal in the 18th century, a once-bustling hub of trade and administration on the Bhagirathi; today it is a heritage city of palaces, mosques and cemeteries ~200 km from Kolkata, famed for the Hazarduari Palace and silk craft.

travel.railway: Murshidabad railway station (~1.5-3 km from the mosque)
travel.road: ~200 km by road from Kolkata; autos and taxis from Murshidabad station
